title: AWS API MCP Server -- T1562.001 a startup policy-load failure silently disables the per-request security-policy gate for the process lifetime
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-16584 (GHSA-29w2-fq35-v728),
affecting `awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server` >= 0.2.13 and < 1.3.47.

`SecurityPolicy._load_policy()` in
`awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/core/security/policy.py` reads the
operator-configured deny/gate policy file at startup inside a
try/except that, on any parse or read failure, calls
`logger.error('Failed to load security policy from {}: {}',
policy_path, e)` and then simply continues -- the denylist and elicit
list stay at their empty initial values, and nothing downstream
checks whether the load actually succeeded. The per-request policy
check that consults these lists is then silently skipped for the
entire lifetime of the process: configured deny and gate rules are
never enforced, and AWS API operations the operator intended to
restrict execute without that gate. The underlying IAM permissions on
the configured credentials remain in effect and continue to bound
what the server can do -- this is specifically a bypass of the
policy-file gate layered on top of IAM, not of IAM itself.

Detection logic flags the exact logged failure message
`Failed to load security policy from` at MCP server startup -- the
literal signal this advisory's source confirms is emitted when the
vulnerable version enters the silently-unenforced state -- as a
precondition alert requiring operator investigation into whether the
degraded process is still serving requests.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (AWS, via
GHSA and NVD) plus the actual current source
(`awslabs/mcp:src/aws-api-mcp-server/.../core/security/policy.py`)
confirming the exact log message text this rule matches on, fixed in
1.3.47.
